summary: The stale-opener version re-check was applied only to the 6->7, 7->8, 8->9 and fresh-create rungs; the 1->2, 2->3, 3->4, 4->5 and 5->6 rungs still write user_version unconditionally, so a stale opener downgrades and re-climbs a current store.
failure_scenario: Process A and B both read user_version 5 (or 2/3/4). A climbs the store to 9 and commits runs, acks, disposals. B then reaches _migrate_m5_to_m6 (executescript commits and drops the write lock, no version re-read under lock) and executes PRAGMA user_version = 6. The next opener re-climbs 6->7 over a v9 store: m6->m7 re-stamps every ack as legacy and re-seals, m7->m8 then refuses ('schema 7 already carries current capability accounting structure'). The store is permanently bricked, or partly rewritten with data (m6->m7 'partly migrated' contradiction), with no heal-on-open per ADR 0016. m3->m4 additionally rewrites lease scope/state/disposition rows of the current store. Also the user_version >= 9 gate on disposal projection (_sqlite_execution_facts.stored_event_from_row, _validate_v7_fact_inventory) means a downgrade to 8 makes disposal events unprojected and m8->m9 refuses on them.
evidence: Executed: created a current v9 store, then called j._migrate_m5_to_m6(conn), _migrate_m4_to_m5, _migrate_m3_to_m4, _migrate_m2_to_m3 directly on it (the state a stale opener holds). PRAGMA user_version went 9 -> 6 -> 5 -> 4 -> 3 with no refusal; the following SqliteJournal(path) raised JournalDamaged 'schema 7 already carries current capability accounting structure' after m6->m7 had already run and committed. Read: _migrate_m4_to_m5/_migrate_m5_to_m6 (lines 489, 1124) have no version re-read; _migrate_m2_to_m3 (1346) takes no BEGIN IMMEDIATE; _migrate_m3_to_m4 (1367) and _migrate_m1_to_m2 (1258) take the lock but never re-read user_version. tests/migrations/test_migration_races.py covers only the m6->m7 loser; test_sqlite_v7_to_v8.py has an m7->m8 loser test; no m8->m9 loser test exists in test_sqlite_v8_to_v9.py. This is an incomplete fix of the recorded race (same class, other rungs), pre-existing for rungs <=5 and the missing m8->m9 loser coverage.

summary: _downgrade_v7_schema_to_v6 fabricates 'schema-6' stores from a current-writer database, so v4/v5/v6 migration tests, race tests and graph-migration tests run on already-modern row shapes the historical writers could not produce, contradicting historical_sqlite.py's stated law.
failure_scenario: The helper drops v7 columns/tables and sets user_version = 6 but keeps current-writer rows: a lease created through the current writer leaves a LeaseAcquired event with payload observed_at, which the real schema-6 fixture (schema6-initial-lifecycle.sql, actual writer 181672a) does not have; current run/effect/command bytes are likewise kept. Migration paths that classify 'current-shaped event in legacy history' (e.g. 'opaque historical' refusal) or that seal legacy leases then see inputs no old writer wrote, so a migration bug on genuine v6 bytes (or an over-accepting classification) is invisible, and refusals are tested against impossible states. test_sqlite_v4_to_v5, test_sqlite_v5_to_v6, test_sqlite_v7_graph_migration, test_sqlite_v7_inventory, test_historical_promotion_authority, test_v6_scalar_collisions and test_migration_races all derive their 'historical' store this way; the v4->v5 and v5->v6 tests also only DROP tables and set user_version.
evidence: Executed: current store with one lease -> _downgrade_v7_schema_to_v6 -> user_version 6 and events row 2 = LeaseAcquired payload containing "observed_at" (v7 shape) while the committed v6 fixture's LeaseAcquired payloads contain none. tests/migrations/historical_sqlite.py docstring says tests 'never create a current database and pretend an older user_version makes its rows historical'; that is exactly what these tests do. Pre-existing structure; the committed SQL fixtures are the only genuine-writer sources.

summary: The three 'actual writer' fixtures contain only runs, one manifest, events and capability leases: every other durable family (commands, approvals, effects, checkpoints, attestations, promotions, components, channel messages/acks, run_origins) is empty, so the v6->v7->v8->v9 climb is never exercised on genuine historical bytes for those families.
failure_scenario: A migration bug that mis-seals or misclassifies a real schema-6 channel ack/reply, command plan envelope, effect terminal row or promotion passes CI because those rows exist only via the current-writer downgrade helper (finding above). Likewise schema7/schema8 fixtures have exactly one lost lease at epoch 1 (v7) and two active leases (v8): no closed/dispositioned lease, no acquisition_epoch > 1 after reclaim, no effect-event/checkpoint pairs, so epoch-fence and disposition inventory logic at the v7/v8 floors is covered only on synthetic inputs. The v6 fixture's closed and lost leases are born that way by one LeaseAcquired event (writer API admitted, a real runtime acquires active), so the 'initial lost' witness path rests on a shape whose real-runtime reachability is not demonstrated.
evidence: Read all three .sql files: INSERT statements exist only for capability_leases, events, manifests, runs, durable_fact_seals, capability_accounting_eras, channel_provenance. Generator _capability_history.py only creates runs and leases. Provenance claims (writer SHAs 181672a, dfd116b) cannot be checked: git history here is shallow (50 commits, those objects absent) -- unverified.

summary: Fixture bytes and provenance are not pinned or regenerable in CI: no test hashes the committed SQL, the generator is never imported or run, and every timestamp in all fixtures is the single frozen instant 2026-01-01T00:00:00+00:00.
failure_scenario: A hand-edit of a fixture (or a regenerate that changes seals) silently redefines the 'historical era' under test, while its header still claims an actual pinned writer. Because created_at, observed_at, updated_at and heartbeat are all identical, comparisons between lease updated_at, event created_at and the legacy-seal updated_at (the legacy_seal.updated_at / last_observed_at checks) can never distinguish a swapped, reordered or stale timestamp, so timestamp-coupled guards are not exercised on fixture data. The disposal-baseline shape is also not an independent schema-8 store: it is the schema-7 fixture opened by the 8 writer, then extended, and the generator imports the current checkout's tests.run_worlds helpers.
evidence: grep for the fixture names shows only functional use; no hash/digest assertion over tests/fixtures/capability_history/*.sql. Generator header says 'Not imported by tests'. All INSERT timestamps in the three files are identical. Verified by reading; not executed against an old writer (objects absent).

summary: The promotion-authority test only exercises acceptance of a mismatched-creator historical promotion; the matching refusals (subject/component/version/endpoint contradictions) are not pinned in this file, and the 'exact early M6' bytes are built with the current attestation writer.
failure_scenario: If the historical promotion authority check were weakened to accept any attestation for any promotion (only the creator-mismatch relaxation is intended), this file would still pass. Behaviour today is correct: mutating to_version, component, from_version or channel of the same row makes SqliteJournal() refuse with JournalDamaged.
evidence: Executed a variant of the test with mutated promotion rows: baseline ACCEPT; to_version differs REFUSE ('contradicts its authority fact'); component differs REFUSE; bogus from_version REFUSE ('registry cut exposes promotion endpoints'); channel 'canary' REFUSE. Whether another test file pins these is unverified.

summary: Mutating the schema7 and schema8 fixtures (delete/alter lease rows, lost->active/closed, resource_ref/binding/epoch/scope/lifetime/updated_at changes, era floor, run status) is refused with JournalDamaged from the intended event-chain, legacy-seal or era-seal guards; unmodified fixtures open and reach v9. Executed.

test_eventless_legacy_erasure_refuses_even_with_valid_event_extent reaches the intended accounting-floor/era-missing guards for all six state/erase_era cases (messages: 'accounting inventory ... changed at its floor' / 'accounting era ... is missing'), though its match regex 'accounting|inventory|era|lost' is looser than needed. Executed.

_sqlite_fact_seals.py: seal identity is bound into the stored hash by sealed_fact_hash, key/selector split rows and family mismatches raise JournalDamaged, store is write-once with proof of prior exact seal; inventory check requires known family and exact count. No defect found. Read only.

_sqlite_execution_facts.py: event/checkpoint seals use canonical exact-position keys with strict int/str type checks; resume-attempt relationship is a checked bijection; checkpoint/completion-event one-to-one inventory is enforced. Only concern is the user_version>=9 gate (covered in the first finding). Read only.

_migrate_m6_to_m7, _migrate_m7_to_m8 and _migrate_m8_to_m9 re-read user_version under BEGIN IMMEDIATE, validate inventory before publishing user_version, and are atomic (crash tests before/after commit exist for 7->8 and 8->9); m8->m9 refuses non-empty disposal baselines. Read; the 8->9 refusal cases are covered by tests that were read, not executed.
